# Implementation Plan: Enable & Validate codex-engine Ralph Members (Spike)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/plan.md`.*

## Overview

This is an **enablement + validation SPIKE** (scope=crews), not a feature build. The goal is to make a
`--engine codex` crews member able to run a *real* ralph workflow (`/brainstorm-with-ralph` or a tiny
`/plan-with-ralph`) end-to-end on this Windows box, OR enumerate the blockers with root causes and a
concrete remediation path. The single durable deliverable is a **findings doc**; the spike de-risks and
feeds the downstream `crews-target-engine-plugin-provisioning` automation design.

The seed framed this as "ralph-orchestration is NOT installed in codex; install it." Ground-truth
verification on 2026-06-07 **corrected that**: ralph-orchestration is ALREADY installed in codex
(cache v5.50.0), crews is installed (v3.6.2), and only ralph-overview is absent. The codex installs are
simply STALE vs the local-source marketplace (crews 3.12.0 / ralph 5.52.0). So the spike is a
*refresh-stale + verify + validate + document* exercise. Critically, the spike **discovered the real
blocker is not installation at all** — it is that ralph ships no codex-flavored skill overlay and codex
lacks three harness primitives (skill chaining, typed subagents, streaming background output) that ralph
skills depend on. Those gaps are already scoped in `codex/tasks/prd-plugin-parity-skill-agent-streaming.md`.

This plan does NOT change any plugin code and does NOT bump any version. It sequences the live install +
verification + validation as stories the impl phase executes, and specifies the findings doc those stories
produce. The remediation work itself (a `.codex-plugin` ralph overlay and/or codex engine parity) is OUT
of scope and is surfaced as follow-up candidates.

**Realistic expected outcome (avoid over-claiming).** Given the research below, the END-TO-END "a codex
member completes a real ralph phase" outcome is EXPECTED to be only partially reached: install/refresh +
fresh-thread skill advertisement + the crews codex MEMBER LIFECYCLE should work, but the ralph SKILL bodies
are Claude-flavored and codex lacks typed subagents / skill chaining / streaming, so `/brainstorm-with-ralph`
and `/plan-with-ralph` will likely degrade. The spike therefore treats the **enumerated-blockers findings
doc as the primary, expected deliverable**, and a fully-green end-to-end run as a bonus, not the bar. The
acceptance is an explicit OR at the outcome level (works end-to-end OR blockers enumerated), with the
findings doc required in BOTH branches.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

- **Crews launcher fix is shipped (lead-side gate cleared).** `plugins/crews/hooks/actors.js:181-229` &
  `:285-302` emit `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for the codex `skipPerms` branch (crews
  v3.6.4) and drop the fatal `--add-dir`. The lead runs Copilot crews **v3.12.0** (has the fix), so a
  `--engine codex` member CAN start, gated on a trusted/skipPermissions spawn. Retires the
  `crews-codex-member-spawn-does-not-start-session` blocker at the launcher layer.
- **Two crews installs are in play.** (a) the lead's Copilot crews 3.12.0 builds the `codex …` launcher
  command; (b) the codex member's OWN codex-cached crews (3.6.2) provides its SessionStart / PreToolUse /
  Stop / listener hooks once it starts. (b) is stale and must be refreshed for the member lifecycle to
  match current behavior.
- **Codex loads plugins from a per-version cache copy**, not the source dir
  (`~/.codex/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`; codex/CLAUDE.md "Plugin source edits do NOT
  propagate to the marketplace cache"). Current cache (verified): `crews/3.6.2`, `ralph-orchestration/5.50.0`,
  no ralph-overview. `codex plugin add <plugin>@ai-developer-toolkit` re-copies current source into a new
  version subdir. **A fresh codex thread is required after install/update** to pick up skills/hooks/MCP.
- **Marketplace `ai-developer-toolkit` is local-source** (root `D:\harness-efforts\codexu\ai-developer-toolkit`),
  structurally immune to the codex git-marketplace auto-upgrade corruption bug
  (`.ralph/investigations/codex-git-marketplace-snapshot-tmp-ephemeral`). NEVER use a git-source marketplace.
- **ralph has NO codex skill/tool-name overlay.** Layout is `.claude-plugin/` (source skills, Claude-flavored
  `Agent`/`Skill`/`Bash`/`EnterPlanMode`/`run_in_background`) + `.copilot-plugin/` (Copilot `task`/`bash`).
  No `.codex-plugin/`, no codex-*.js hooks. Codex discovers `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` first then falls
  back to `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + the default `skills/` root — so a codex member loads the
  CLAUDE-FLAVORED bodies. crews, by contrast, ships `plugins/crews/.codex-plugin/{plugin.json,hooks/hooks.json}`
  + `hooks/codex-*.js`, which is why crews codex members register/listen.
- **Ralph bash-orientation is mostly stale.** ralph v5.46.0 deleted ALL `.sh` runtime; production is pure
  Node ESM (`node src/*.mjs`); `jq` is not required at runtime; the ~23 surviving `.sh` are TESTS only.
  So `/plan-with-ralph` / `/brainstorm-with-ralph` runtime is cross-platform `node`, not bash — this
  meaningfully de-risks the seed's "ralph bash-orientation" concern.
- **The harness-aware seam is artifact generation.** `plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs`
  (18-entry substitution table, applied to `.copilot-plugin/*` only; agent bodies engine-neutral) is the
  existing pattern; there is no codex generator/overlay. The repo's "harness-aware plugins" convention says
  to EXTEND this seam per-harness rather than build a runtime translation adapter.

### Technical Constraints

- **Codex lacks three harness primitives ralph depends on**, all scoped in
  `codex/tasks/prd-plugin-parity-skill-agent-streaming.md`: (F1) skill chaining / `invoke_skill` +
  `internal:true`; (F2) typed subagent spawning (`Agent({subagent_type})`); (F3) streaming background output
  (`Monitor` over `Bash(run_in_background)`, used by crews listeners). Codex ALREADY has the full hook
  surface, Claude-compat tool aliases (shell→Bash, apply_patch→Write/Edit), `request_user_input`≡`AskUserQuestion`,
  and the `.codex-plugin/` marketplace + manifest. So even a tool-name overlay cannot, by itself, make
  `/plan-with-ralph`'s parallel research fan-out or `/implement-with-ralph`'s skill chaining work — those need
  F1/F2/F3.
- **`/brainstorm-with-ralph` is NOT a primitive-free workflow.** Its SKILL.md
  (`plugins/ralph/skills/brainstorm-with-ralph/SKILL.md`) uses Claude-flavored `Agent(... run_in_background)`
  + background `Bash` lenses, i.e. it leans on the same F2/F3 primitives codex lacks. It is "lightest" only
  in fan-out breadth, NOT in primitive dependency. Therefore it CANNOT serve as a clean crews-codex-membership
  test: a brainstorm failure can't distinguish "crews codex member is broken" from "ralph primitive missing."
  The crews member lifecycle MUST be validated by a separate primitive-free smoke (a bare member that just
  arms its listener and emits a `kind=done` report, no ralph) BEFORE any ralph skill is invoked.
- **codex-exec recursion reliability is a live risk on this box.** During THIS plan's Phase 2, the
  `codex-exec.mjs` research lens (xhigh) hung > 20 min past its 300s timeout and produced nothing, while
  `copilot-exec.mjs` completed cleanly in ~5 min. A codex member running `/plan-with-ralph` Phase 2/4 would
  invoke `codex-exec.mjs` (codex-inside-codex) and could hit the same hang.
- Read-only snapshot guard is HARD-DISABLED in ralph v5.52.0 (`READONLY_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED=false`, OOM
  mitigation against the 21GB gitignored `codex-rs/target`), so concurrent read-only lenses won't OOM, but
  `codex-exec` runs `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (write-capable, no revert guard).
- **Windows landmines** (codexu AGENTS.md): MAX_PATH on deep `.ralph/jobs/<slug>/worktree/` paths; PS 5.1
  encoding for `.ps1`; WSL-`bash`-on-PATH can hang `spawnSync('bash')`; MSYS path conversion mangles refs.
- ralph-orchestration ships **no MCP server** (skills-only); brainstorm/plan/impl don't need overview MCP,
  so ralph-overview install is optional (only to test overview MCP under codex).

## Approach

### Architecture

A strictly **sequential validation probe** that fails fast at the earliest broken gate and records WHAT
broke + the root cause at each gate, accumulating into one findings doc. No plugin/engine code changes;
the only system mutations are codex plugin-cache refreshes (reversible via reinstall) and one throwaway
ralph job on a throwaway task. The lightest real workflow (`/brainstorm-with-ralph`, which halts for a
user choice and has the smallest fan-out) is the primary validation target; a tiny `/plan-with-ralph` is a
secondary probe specifically to characterize the F1/F2/F3 primitive gaps.

### Implementation Strategy

Gates, in order (each is a story; later gates may be short-circuited by an earlier hard failure, in which
case the findings doc records the blocking gate and the remaining gates are marked NOT-REACHED with the
reason):

1. **Refresh codex plugin cache from local source.** First capture a PRE-state snapshot (the cache version
   subdirs under `~/.codex/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/` and the relevant `[plugins."*@ai-developer-toolkit"]`
   stanzas in `~/.codex/config.toml`). Then `codex plugin add crews@ai-developer-toolkit` (→3.12.0) and
   `codex plugin add ralph-orchestration@ai-developer-toolkit` (→5.52.0); optionally
   `codex plugin add ralph-overview@ai-developer-toolkit`. **Install/enablement evidence is the cache version
   subdirs (`~/.codex/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/<plugin>/<version>/`) + the enabled stanzas in
   `~/.codex/config.toml`, NOT `codex plugin list`** (which lists marketplace-snapshot availability, not
   active install state). Capture a POST-state snapshot. Re-approve hook trust if codex prompts on the next
   fresh thread.
2. **Restart into a fresh codex thread/session (explicit precondition gate).** Plugin-cache refreshes do NOT
   affect an already-open codex session — skills/hooks/MCP only reload on a NEW thread. This gate exists so a
   stale session never masquerades as a refresh failure. The verification in gate 3 MUST run in a thread
   started AFTER gate 1.
3. **Verify skill advertisement/loading.** In the fresh codex thread, confirm whether `ralph-orchestration:*`
   skills are advertised. **Capture method must be explicit**: save the codex session's skill-discovery output
   (startup skill-list system reminder and/or the `/`-command listing) as a transcript excerpt into the
   findings doc, and record whether codex resolved the skills via the `.codex-plugin` path (absent for ralph)
   or the `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` fallback + default `skills/` root. Note that "advertised" ≠ "executes
   correctly" — that distinction is the whole point of gates 5-6.
4. **Validate the crews codex MEMBER lifecycle in ISOLATION (primitive-free smoke, no ralph).** From the lead,
   spawn a `--engine codex` member on a THROWAWAY task whose prompt is "arm your listener and emit a
   `kind=done` report with a one-line summary; do NOT run any ralph skill." Observe gate-by-gate: member
   starts (launcher gate); codex fires the crews `codex-session-start.js` → arms the listener; the member
   emits a `kind=done` that reaches the lead mailbox; `/crews:stop-member` cleanly closes the tab. This
   isolates "does crews-codex membership work?" from "do ralph primitives work?". **Autonomous-vs-interactive
   driving contract:** the member runs as an interactive `codex` TUI in a `wt.exe` tab. If, on this box, the
   spawn/observe/stop loop cannot be driven autonomously by the impl agent (e.g. it requires a human to watch
   the tab or answer a codex trust prompt), the impl agent MUST record the exact interactive-driving blocker
   and STOP this gate with that finding — it does NOT silently hang or loop. The lead/operator may then drive
   the spawn manually and the impl agent records the observed result. Either way the outcome is captured.
5. **Attempt the lightest real ralph workflow (`/brainstorm-with-ralph`) — only after gate 4 passes.** Have a
   codex member attempt `/brainstorm-with-ralph` on a trivial throwaway idea. Because brainstorm uses
   `Agent(... run_in_background)` + background `Bash` lenses (F2/F3), this is EXPECTED to degrade; the
   objective is to capture how far it gets and the exact failure point (which tool call / what codex emits).
   Hard timebox: 10 minutes; on timeout/hang, kill and record NOT-COMPLETED with the captured tail.
6. **Degradation probe — tiny `/plan-with-ralph` (characterize the F1/F2/F3 gap).** Attempt a tiny throwaway
   `/plan-with-ralph` to probe the typed-subagent fan-out (F2) and skill-chaining (F1). **Hard timebox: 10
   minutes** (the codex-exec recursion hang observed this session makes an unbounded run dangerous). Save
   stdout/stderr/transcript excerpts into the findings doc; if it does not start or hangs, mark NOT-REACHED /
   HUNG with the captured evidence and the blocking earlier gate.
7. **Produce the findings doc** at `.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/findings.md`: a
   works/partially-works/breaks matrix across {plugin install/refresh, fresh-thread skill advertisement,
   crews codex member start, listener/Stop-hook lifecycle, `/brainstorm-with-ralph` execution, `/plan-with-ralph`
   execution, codex-exec recursion, MCP}; each row with a root cause and a remediation pointer; the PRE/POST
   codex cache+config snapshots from gate 1; and the two remediation tracks (below) cross-referencing
   `codex/tasks/prd-plugin-parity-skill-agent-streaming.md` and the downstream `crews-target-engine-plugin-provisioning`
   design. **Then CLEAN UP the throwaway artifacts** (delete the throwaway job/brainstorm dirs created in gates
   4-6 — they live under the TRACKED `.ralph/jobs/` & `.ralph/brainstorms/` trees, so leaving them would commit
   spike scratch) so the final committed diff is exactly `findings.md` (+ the optional one-line fork-roadmap
   pointer). Cite the live transcript inside `findings.md` instead of committing the throwaway dirs.
8. **Capture codex/Windows operational notes** discovered along the way (cache-not-source refresh semantics,
   fresh-thread-required, `codex plugin list` ≠ install state, bash-tests-only, codex-exec hang, MAX_PATH on
   deep worktree paths, interactive-spawn driving) into the findings doc's operations section so future
   sessions don't re-derive them.

**Two remediation tracks (documented, NOT implemented in this spike):**
- **Track A — plugin-side codex overlay.** Extend `plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs`
  with a codex substitution table and emit a `.codex-plugin/` overlay for ralph (mirroring the crews codex
  overlay), translating `Agent(...)`/`Skill(...)`/`Bash(...)`/`EnterPlanMode`/`run_in_background` to codex
  equivalents. Makes the skill BODIES codex-native. Bounded plugin work, but cannot conjure missing codex
  PRIMITIVES.
- **Track B — engine-side parity.** Implement `codex/tasks/prd-plugin-parity-skill-agent-streaming.md`
  Features 1-3 (`invoke_skill`+`internal:true`, typed subagents, streaming background output). Heavy codex
  Rust work; the only way to make skill chaining + typed fan-out actually run under codex.
  The spike's job is to map which ralph workflows need only A, which need A+B, and which already work with
  neither (the crews member lifecycle, expected to work after the refresh).

### Files to Create/Modify

This spike creates exactly ONE durable repo artifact plus the standard ralph job dir; it modifies NO plugin
or engine source.

- CREATE `.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/findings.md` — the findings doc (primary deliverable).
- CREATE/UPDATE (optional, if a durable pointer is useful) a one-line entry in `docs/fork-roadmap.md`
  follow-ups referencing the two remediation tracks + this findings doc. (Fork-level docs go in codexu;
  do NOT touch the gitignored CLAUDE.md.)
- TRANSIENT (must be cleaned up before the final commit): codex plugin-cache version subdirs under
  `~/.codex/plugins/cache/...` (outside the repo — not in the diff); and one throwaway ralph job/brainstorm
  under `.ralph/jobs/` or `.ralph/brainstorms/` for the throwaway task. **These `.ralph/jobs/` &
  `.ralph/brainstorms/` trees are TRACKED in codexu (only their `worktree/` subdirs are gitignored), so the
  throwaway dirs MUST be deleted before the final commit** — otherwise they would land in the diff. Capture
  any needed transcript excerpts INTO `findings.md` first, then delete the throwaway dirs.
- NO edits to `plugins/ralph/**`, `plugins/crews/**`, or `codex/**` in this spike. Final committed diff =
  `findings.md` (+ optional one-line `docs/fork-roadmap.md` follow-up) ONLY.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Refreshing the stale codex plugin-cache installs (crews, ralph-orchestration; optional ralph-overview)
  from the LOCAL-SOURCE marketplace via `codex plugin add`.
- Verifying codex advertises/loads the ralph skills after a fresh thread.
- A live end-to-end validation of a `--engine codex` crews member running the lightest real ralph workflow
  (`/brainstorm-with-ralph`) plus a degradation probe of a tiny `/plan-with-ralph`.
- Documenting works/breaks + root causes + a remediation path in a findings doc.

### Out of Scope
- Implementing a `.codex-plugin` ralph overlay or a codex artifact generator (Track A) — follow-up.
- Implementing codex engine parity Features 1-3 (Track B) — follow-up, owned by the codex submodule.
- Any plugin version bump or marketplace-index edit.
- Fixing the codex-exec recursion hang.
- ralph-overview MCP-under-codex validation beyond an optional install (brainstorm/plan don't need it).
- Driving `/implement-with-ralph` under codex (heaviest chaining; out of a de-risking spike).

## Risk Areas

- **Interactive wt.exe TUI spawn may not be autonomously driveable.** A `--engine codex` member is an
  interactive `codex` TUI in a `wt.exe` tab; the spawn/observe/stop loop may require a human to watch the tab
  or answer a first-run codex trust prompt. Mitigation: gate 4 defines an explicit fallback — if the impl
  agent can't drive it autonomously, record the exact interactive-driving blocker and STOP that gate (no
  silent hang); the operator drives the spawn manually and the agent records the observed result.
- **Throwaway artifacts would pollute the committed diff.** `.ralph/jobs/` & `.ralph/brainstorms/` are tracked
  in codexu (only `worktree/` is gitignored), so a throwaway job/brainstorm left behind would be committed.
  Mitigation: gate 7 mandates capturing transcript excerpts into `findings.md` then deleting the throwaway
  dirs before the final commit.
- **Global codex state mutation without snapshots.** The refresh mutates `~/.codex/plugins/cache` and possibly
  `~/.codex/config.toml` (hook trust). Mitigation: gate 1 captures PRE/POST snapshots into the findings doc so
  the change is auditable and reversible (reinstall the prior version / restore the stanza).
- **Stale codex crews (3.6.2) member hooks may misbehave** even after a launcher start — the codex-side
  SessionStart/Stop/PreToolUse hooks predate many fixes. Mitigation: the FIRST story refreshes crews to
  3.12.0; the lifecycle validation (story 3) runs only after the refresh + a fresh thread.
- **Trusted-spawn requirement.** The launcher only emits the bypass flag when `skipPermissions` is set;
  a non-trusted codex spawn falls back to `--sandbox read-only` and the member can't write `~/.crews`
  (heartbeat/mailbox). The spawn must be a trusted/skipPermissions spawn. Verify the crews spawn default.
- **codex-exec recursion hang** (observed this session) can stall the `/plan-with-ralph` probe (story 4).
  Mitigation: time-box story 4; treat a hang as a recorded finding, not a failure of the spike.
- **Fresh-thread requirement** — skills/hooks/MCP don't refresh in an already-open codex session after
  `codex plugin add`. Every verification must start a new codex thread.
- **Windows MAX_PATH** on the deep `.ralph/jobs/<slug>/worktree/` path the member may use; keep the
  throwaway job's paths short, or run the throwaway brainstorm from a shallow cwd.
- **No-op risk / false "works"**: codex advertising a skill is NOT the same as executing it correctly.
  Story 2 (advertised) and story 3/4 (executed) are distinct gates; the findings matrix must not conflate them.
- **Cleanup**: refreshing leaves old cache version subdirs (3.6.2 / 5.50.0) behind; record whether they
  should be pruned (codex active-version selection picks the new dir, so leaving them is safe). The throwaway
  TASK artifacts under `.ralph/jobs/`/`.ralph/brainstorms/` MUST be removed before the final commit (see the
  throwaway-artifacts risk above), not merely marked.

## Acceptance Criteria

The spike is DONE when ALL of the following hold (note the acceptance is intentionally an OR at the outcome
level: a working end-to-end run OR an enumerated-blockers findings doc — but the findings doc is required
either way):

- [ ] codex plugin cache shows crews ≥3.12.0 and ralph-orchestration ≥5.52.0 after `codex plugin add` from
      the local-source marketplace, verified by the cache version subdirs
      (`~/.codex/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/<plugin>/<version>/`) and the enabled stanzas in
      `~/.codex/config.toml` (NOT `codex plugin list`, which reports marketplace availability, not install
      state). PRE/POST snapshots of cache + config captured into the findings doc.
- [ ] A fresh codex thread/session was started AFTER the refresh, and its skill advertisement is captured by
      an explicit method — a saved transcript excerpt of codex's skill-discovery output / `/`-command listing
      pasted into the findings doc — recording whether `ralph-orchestration:*` skills appear and whether they
      resolved via the `.claude-plugin` fallback + default `skills/` root.
- [ ] A primitive-free crews codex member smoke (NO ralph) was run: a `--engine codex` member was spawned by
      the lead and the lifecycle outcome is recorded gate-by-gate (started? `codex-session-start.js` armed the
      listener? `kind=done` reached the lead mailbox? clean `/crews:stop-member`?). If the wt.exe TUI spawn
      could not be driven autonomously, the exact interactive-driving blocker is recorded and the operator's
      manual-driving result is captured — the gate is never left as a silent hang.
- [ ] The `/brainstorm-with-ralph` attempt (after the lifecycle smoke) is recorded gate-by-gate with its exact
      failure/degradation point and a 10-minute timebox honored (NOT-COMPLETED + captured tail on timeout).
- [ ] The `/plan-with-ralph` degradation probe's exact failure mode (or hang) is recorded as evidence for the
      F1/F2/F3 primitive gaps, with a 10-minute hard timebox and saved stdout/stderr/transcript excerpts, or
      marked NOT-REACHED/HUNG with the blocking earlier gate.
- [ ] `findings.md` exists at the job dir with: a works/partially/breaks matrix, a root cause per broken
      row, the PRE/POST codex cache+config snapshots, the two remediation tracks (A plugin overlay, B engine
      parity) with concrete file pointers, and cross-references to
      `codex/tasks/prd-plugin-parity-skill-agent-streaming.md` and `crews-target-engine-plugin-provisioning`.
- [ ] codex/Windows operational notes (cache-not-source, fresh-thread, `codex plugin list`≠install-state,
      bash-tests-only, codex-exec hang, MAX_PATH, interactive-spawn driving) are captured in the findings doc.
- [ ] Throwaway task artifacts under `.ralph/jobs/`/`.ralph/brainstorms/` were deleted before the final
      commit; no plugin/engine source was modified and no version was bumped (final diff = `findings.md` +
      optional one-line `docs/fork-roadmap.md` follow-up ONLY).

## Suggested Decomposition

This is a sequential live-probe spike: each gate's outcome is the input to the next, and they all mutate /
observe the same single codex environment + the same findings doc. There is no safe parallelism — the
stories share the codex plugin cache, one codex environment, and one `findings.md`. Run as ONE serial cluster.

### Cluster: codex-engine-validation-probe
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/findings.md`, the single
  codex plugin cache `~/.codex/plugins/cache/...`, one codex environment]; exclusive=[]; risk=high
- `execution_mode` rationale: Every story reads/writes the same codex environment and the same findings doc,
  and each gate's result gates the next; parallelizing would corrupt the shared cache state and the findings
  narrative. Strictly serial.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/suggested-decomposition.json`
(Note: a single serial cluster — the parallel handoff is provided for contract completeness but this spike
should run serially.)
